clue.text: Difficult, like a granny

definitions.meaning: hard to untangle or solve, as a tricky problem is
having the quality of a granny knot, a familiar (if insecure) way of tying a rope

explanation.walkthrough: 'Granny' looks like an old woman, but here it is the granny knot, so the second definition means full of knots.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny, complicated problem is described with this word, and a rope tied in granny knots literally fits it too.

clue.text: Christine covers new church cushion

indicators.note: covers means the surname wraps around the letter for new

parts.note: Christine Keeler was the model at the centre of the 1963 Profumo affair

explanation.surface: Christine is reupholstering a fresh pew cushion for the church.
explanation.walkthrough: Christine Keeler was the woman at the heart of Britain's 1963 Profumo political scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad placed in pews for worshippers to kneel on during prayer.

clue.text: Open set of deliveries on time

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket over is bowled on schedule in front of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an OVER is a set of six deliveries from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in plain sight and not hidden, as an obvious act of hostility is.

clue.text: Journeyman referee shut up by narrator?

indicators.note: shut, with by, means the narrator's word encloses the turned piece

parts.note: a teller is one who narrates a story

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the referee's letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: VAR is the video assistant referee in football

explanation.surface: An itinerant worker who acts as referee is silenced by a storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: The referee is football's video assistant referee; 'up' reads it bottom to top, as suits a down clue, and 'shut ... by' has the storyteller close round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A journeyman is literally one who journeys, a wayfarer making a trip.

clue.text: Eg cello playing taught here

indicators.note: playing suggests the cello being played, but it signals the letters of eg cello being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes that cello performance is one of the subjects on offer at this institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges EG and CELLO, seven letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is an institution of learning, so it is a place where lessons are taught.

clue.text: Manage to study most of offensive poster

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the poster's word is dropped

parts.note: a troll posts deliberately offensive messages online

explanation.surface: A moderator tries to handle a hostile online commenter by studying them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' looks like a placard, but here it is someone who posts online.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage something is to direct or have command of it.

clue.text: Let lake calm down

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
to ease is to calm or relieve

explanation.surface: An instruction to let a lake settle and grow still.
explanation.definitionFit: To rent out a property is to let it, granting a tenancy.

clue.text: Passionate outpouring on to email

indicators.note: outpouring suggests feelings spilling out, signalling that on to email is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone vents their feelings in a heartfelt email.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outpouring' rearranges ONTOEMAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of strong feeling, as an impassioned speech is.

clue.text: Final tree to be seen in 2050-60?

parts.note: final means end
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Someone predicts the last tree will be spotted in the 2050s.
explanation.walkthrough: '2050-60' looks like a future decade, but the clue points at the punctuation mark joining the two numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The short typographic line placed between numbers in a range is this mark.

clue.text: A second medal?

parts.note: reads as an extra medal, but means the award given to the runner-up in second place

explanation.definitionFit: Runners-up at the Olympics receive a medal made of this metal.

clue.text: Given promotion, delight in receiving modern car

indicators.note: receiving means the word for delight takes in the car's letters

parts.note: delight means elation
EV, an electric vehicle, is the modern kind of car

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at being promoted gets a new electric car as a perk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' is only a link word; EV, short for electric vehicle, is the crossword's modern car, held by 'receiving'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being raised to a higher rank at work is a rise in status, a lifting up.

clue.text: Permitted to speak for all to hear

indicators.note: to speak means the word for permitted is pronounced rather than written

parts.note: permitted means allowed

explanation.surface: A speaker is granted the floor so that everyone in the room can listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something audibly, in a voice others can catch, is the plain sense here.

clue.text: Coffee, the second of two not finished

indicators.note: not finished means the final letter of the phrase's synonym is lopped off

parts.note: of two things, the second is the latter

explanation.surface: Asked to choose between two drinks, someone picks the second but leaves it half drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an espresso drink topped with lots of steamed milk.

clue.text: Different types of satire I've recycled

indicators.note: recycled means the letters of satire and I've are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has reworked their old satirical pieces into several new forms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' rearranges SATIRE and IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinds or sorts of a thing are its distinct versions.

clue.text: One on a trail who doesn't get to the point

definitions.meaning: a walker out on a country path or hike

definitions.text: who doesn't get to the point
definitions.meaning: someone who talks on and on, wandering off the subject

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses share the idea of wandering, on foot or in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker roaming the countryside and a long-winded talker both wander aimlessly.

clue.text: People I noted failing to be acknowledged

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: failing suggests the letters of I noted breaking down into a new order

explanation.surface: People noted with dismay that they had not been credited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges INOTED into TIONED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been named or referred to is to have been noted or credited.

clue.text: Starts to lose all confidence, unusually not appreciating gap in text

indicators.note: Starts to means the opening letter of each of the following six words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone loses all self-belief and, oddly, stops valuing what they read.
explanation.definitionFit: A missing portion in a manuscript, where words have been lost, is the scholar's term.

clue.text: Lady Chatterley, not quite assiduous going to church

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter of the word for assiduous is lost

parts.note: assiduous means constant, persistent
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: D. H. Lawrence's heroine is almost devout in her churchgoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' is a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of D. H. Lawrence's novel Lady Chatterley's Lover bears this first name.

clue.text: Girl riding for a fall

indicators.note: for a fall pictures a rider tumbling, signalling that the letters of riding get jumbled

explanation.surface: A young rider is heading for a tumble off her horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a fall' rearranges RIDING.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a girl's given name, as borne by the actress Bergman.

clue.text: Small figures with zero pressure inside become shapeless lumps

indicators.note: inside means the zero and pressure letters go within the word for small figures

parts.note: dolls are small figures of people
O looks like zero
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Little models crushed with no air pressure turn into formless blobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Large spoonfuls of something soft, like mashed potato, plopped down roughly.

clue.text: Messed up, influenced by bribe

parts.note: a bung is British slang for a bribe
influenced means led, as in led astray

explanation.surface: An official made a hash of things after being swayed by a backhander.
explanation.walkthrough: A BUNG is everyday British slang for a bribe or backhander.
explanation.definitionFit: To botch a job is to make a mess of it.

clue.text: Feel confident about request for hamper

indicators.note: about means the word for feel confident goes round the request word

parts.note: to bet is to feel sure, as in I bet
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Someone confidently asks for a picnic hamper.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a wicker container, a large lidded basket.

clue.text: Sort of watch face smashed by fool

indicators.note: smashed by means the fool's word breaks into the face's word

parts.note: a dial is the face of a watch or clock
git is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A watch with its face broken by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: GIT is British slang for a foolish or contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch showing the time as numbers rather than hands is one type.

clue.text: Take off English band

parts.note: to strip is to take off clothes or a covering

explanation.surface: An English group is told to undress.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow band of colour, as on a flag, is this.

clue.text: Work in largest shapes

indicators.note: Work as a verb means knead or shape, so the letters of in and largest are reformed

explanation.surface: An instruction to put something into the biggest available forms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' rearranges IN and LARGEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-sided figures are one family of geometric figures.

clue.text: Pluck cheek

explanation.definitionFit: Courage to act and the brazen audacity to be rude are both this.

clue.text: Item is spare? Good

parts.note: spare as an adjective means lean or thin

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a spare article is any use, then decides it is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare' looks like extra, but here it means lean, as in a spare frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An object or article is a general word for any one item.

clue.text: Expensive block's home purchased

parts.note: in means at home
got means obtained or purchased

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their house cost a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' and links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of cast gold or other precious metal is this costly block.

clue.text: Obscure champion abandoned by wife

indicators.note: abandoned by means the wife's letter leaves the word for champion

parts.note: a champion is a winner

explanation.surface: A little-known title holder has been left by his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden or not obvious, as an inward meaning is that lies below the surface.

clue.text: Finished before dark? By morning

indicators.note: before means the finished word comes ahead of the dark word

parts.note: finished means over
the dark is night-time, the night

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a job will be done before nightfall or only by dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens during the hours of darkness is complete by the next morning.

clue.text: Lacking purpose, but never stopping

definitions.meaning: without an aim or goal, an end in the sense of purpose

explanation.walkthrough: 'end' can mean purpose (to that end), so the first sense reads the word as without an end in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Something interminable goes on for ever, and the word read literally means having no aim.

clue.text: Not heartless in actual charge for room

indicators.note: in means the shortened word goes inside the word for actual

parts.note: actual means real

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of not is removed, keeping first and last

explanation.surface: A complaint that a room rate is not, in fact, unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the middle letter from NOT; the surface reads as a complaint about price, but 'actual' supplies a synonym that 'in' opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: The sum paid to a landlord for use of accommodation is this.
